solution: The Prudential Financial 2024 Annual Report contains a segment reconciliation table in Note 23 of the Consolidated Financial Statements. This table appears on page 216 of the annual report (physical page 217 of the PDF). The table is titled 'Reconciliation of select financial information' and presents revenues and significant benefits and expenses on an adjusted operating income basis for the year ended December 31, 2024.

The reconciliation table lists total revenues for each segment on an adjusted operating income basis. The 'Total segment adjusted operating income before income taxes' row shows total revenues of $68,053 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. This represents total adjusted operating revenues across all segments.

The GAAP total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2024 are reported on the consolidated income statement. The table titled 'Results of Operations' on page 14 of the annual report shows 'Revenues' of $70,405 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. This figure is also confirmed in the segment reconciliation table where the consolidated income before taxes row shows total revenues of $70,405 million.

The difference between adjusted operating revenues and GAAP revenues is $68,053 million minus $70,405 million, which equals negative $2,352 million. Expressed in billions and rounded to the nearest tenth, the difference is negative $2.4 billion.
verification: Note 23 reconciliation table on physical page 217 (printed page 216) shows total segment adjusted operating revenues of $68,053M in the 'Total Revenues' column of the 'Total segment adjusted operating income before income taxes' row. solution: The Chevron 2004 Annual Report (for fiscal year 2003) contains Table III, titled 'Results of Operations for Oil and Gas Producing Activities,' as part of the supplemental oil and gas information. This table appears on physical page 58 of the PDF. The table header states that results are presented in millions of dollars.

Table III for the year ended December 31, 2003 shows the following line items for worldwide operations (including both consolidated companies and affiliated companies): Total revenues from net production of $22,535 million, production expenses and other deductions, and 'Results before income taxes' of $12,475 million in the 'Worldwide' column. This $12,475 million is the worldwide upstream pre-tax earnings for 2003.

The net oil-equivalent production figure for 2003 appears in the production table on physical page 5 of the PDF. The row labeled 'Total Including Affiliates' shows oil-equivalent production of 2,523 thousands of barrels per day (MBOED) for 2003.

To compute total annual barrels produced, multiply 2,523 MBOED by 1,000 (to convert to barrels per day) and by 365 days. This gives 2,523 times 1,000 times 365, which equals 920,895,000 barrels for the year.
The average upstream pre-tax earnings per barrel is $12,475 million divided by 920.895 million barrels. This equals $13.55 per barrel.
verification: Table III on physical page 58 (printed page FS-54 area) shows 'Results before income taxes' for YEAR ENDED DECEMBER 31, 2003 as $12,475M in the Worldwide column (sum: consolidated $11,563M + TCO $867M + Hamaca $45M = $12,475M). Production table on physical page 5 shows 'Total Including Affiliates' of 2,523 MBOED for 2003. Annual barrels = 2,523 x 1,000 x 365 = 920,895,000. Per-barrel pre-tax = $12,475M / 920.895M = $13.55/bbl. The quarantine reason stated the filing 'reports only after-tax segment income' but Table III explicitly discloses pre-tax producing operations results.
